description: Skater body from a third-party STL in the mold frame (scripts/stl-skater.py): origin = fixture axis at the socket underside, +x facing, +y the figure's left; mold units x scale.k_mm_per_mold_unit = mm. PROPOSED: the assets assets/figures/skater_stl_*.glb sit beside the parametric skater; contacts, footprints and traces still use the parametric mold.

source.attribution: STIGA HOCKEY PLAYER by MAVRIS, https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:6898521
source.note: A sculpt of the STIGA skater mold: same pose and handedness as the user's skater no. 21. Used for the body only; its round printable stick is replaced by the traced wire stick.

alignment.method: axis = centre of the base disc (file z < min + 0.2 mm), underside -> z = 0; scale and yaw fitted to the parametric mold (symmetric nearest-point distance clipped at 3 units, stick excluded), so mold units and the fitted photo cameras keep their meaning

scale.source: validation/players/stl/overhead-fit.json: scripts/fit-figure-overhead.py with the STL body (4 Sweden skaters, official overhead at the ASSUMED preview scale)
scale.note: The same overhead fit gives 1.0814 with the parametric mold (skater 51.1 mm). With the STL shape it gives 1.2027: the body is 57.4 mm tall, the STL file's own size x 1.009; the catalog says approx. 57 mm. No ruler measurement of a skater yet.

stick.note: Blade heel/toe and height kept in mm from the traced contact blade (data/geometry.json, official overhead); shaft top in the upper glove (parametric mold point, same mold units); wire radius and blade thickness kept in mm.

runner.note: Metal runner from the ice up into the STL's right boot (boot underside z0 + 0.3 units overlap); ends from the boot underside (vertices within 0.6 units of its lowest point, principal axis). The STL boot floats above the ice by about the runner height.
